sentence: Kayleigh Brennan is the tenant at Flat 4, 18 Cobden Street.
Kayleigh Brennan lives with her children, Alfie (age 7) and Mia (age 3).
Kayleigh Brennan has been living at Flat 4, 18 Cobden Street since the summer of 2021.
The flat is on the top floor and has two bedrooms.
The landlord is Mr Haskins, and the property is managed by agents Kerridge and Lowe.
Kayleigh Brennan is the sole tenant on the tenancy; Liam, her former partner, moved in after and was on a joint Universal Credit claim with her.
Liam moved out on the day after Alfie's birthday, which was the ninth of August.
The tenant (Kayleigh Brennan) stated that if she is evicted, the council would have to rehouse her straight away, according to her understanding.
The housing options officer (Marcus Fenn) stated that the tenant's belief about immediate rehousing upon eviction is incorrect and not how the system works.
The tenant asked whether the agent would know it was her who raised the repair concerns.
The tenant asked when the repair team would come out.
The tenant mentioned that Mrs Patel downstairs said the council came out to her flat last year about damp.
The housing options officer said he will check the building's system for damp issues, but cannot see it from here.
A prevention case was opened today, with statements to be submitted by the tenant by Thursday.
The Department of Health and Social Care (D H P) will submit a statement by Friday the 27th.
The housing options officer said he will contact the agent this week to discuss a rent of fifty pounds per month.
The housing options officer will refer the tenant to private sector housing by the end of the week.
The tenant said 'Okay. Thank you.' at the end of the conversation.
The rent on the flat is currently £895 per month, having increased from £850 in April.
Universal Credit covers £725 for housing per month.
Kayleigh Brennan has a monthly income of £630 from working 12 hours per week at Cobden Road Primary School.
Kayleigh Brennan has no other income, including no child maintenance from Liam, and no savings.
Kayleigh Brennan receives child benefit, which is considered income.
Kayleigh Brennan has reported the damp in the flat multiple times, including by email to the agents (March, June, and 6th October).
The landlord and agent have never visited the property to inspect the damp issues.
The agent's representative (Kerridge's girl) told Kayleigh that Mr Haskins blames the damp on her drying washing in the flat, claiming it is condensation.
Kayleigh Brennan has no dryer and has no alternative place to dry washing.
Moira Quinn from the Brightwater Advice Project stated that the bathroom ceiling leaking is due to a roof issue, not washing.
A plug socket near Alfie's bed sparked last week and is now brown around the edges; Kayleigh has moved the bed to avoid use.
Alfie has asthma and uses his blue inhaler more frequently since the cold weather began.
Alfie is on a waiting list for an autism assessment, with a potential wait of up to 18 months.
Alfie struggles with change and melts down in new environments.
Kayleigh Brennan is currently on sertaline for depression, since the spring.
Kayleigh Brennan skips her tea most nights to ensure her children are fed.
The housing options officer referred the issues of damp, mould, and a faulty socket to the private sector housing team and environmental health.
The housing options officer stated that he cannot give a date for when repairs will be carried out, but will send a referral by the end of the week and repairs will be arranged by
The support worker (Moira Quinn) stated that a disrepair claim for compensation should be considered, specifically for a year of living with a poorly child due to damp.
The housing options officer asked Moira to obtain a GP letter about Alfie's asthma and the damp from Millfield Surgery.
Moira stated she will obtain the GP letter by the fourth of December, noting that the surgery is slow.
The GP letter about Alfie's asthma and damp will be obtained by Moira by the fourth of December.
The tenant stated that she does not want to sue the agent and only wants the issues fixed, and that she would lose the flat if she did so.
The support worker clarified that a disrepair claim is not exactly suing, but a claim for compensation.
The tenant said she does not want to go ahead with a disrepair claim now.
The housing options officer noted that Moira raised the disrepair claim and the tenant declined to proceed with it.
Kayleigh Brennan is behind on rent by £1,960 as of the 2nd of November.
Kayleigh Brennan missed August and September due to a joint claim being closed when Liam moved out, resulting in no housing support during those months.
Mr Haskins has sent a text message on the 17th of November stating that if the arrears are not sorted by the end of the month, he will instruct his solicitor to serve possession.
As of today, no formal notice of possession or solicitor's letter has been received by Kayleigh Brennan.
Kayleigh Brennan and Alfie were admitted to A&E on the 14th of October due to Alfie's asthma exacerbation.
The doctor at the hospital inquired whether there was damp at home and Kayleigh confirmed there was.
No doctor has confirmed that Alfie's asthma is caused by the damp, though Kayleigh believes it may be.
The housing options officer stated that the agent cannot evict the tenant for complaining about repairs.
The housing options officer asked if, in the event of a serious outcome, the tenant could stay with a family member.
The tenant said her mother is in Hull and could potentially stay with her, but she has not yet asked her mother.
The housing options officer said it is not a plan to stay with a family member, just a possibility.
The next meeting with the tenant and housing officer will be on Tuesday the eighth at ten o'clock.
The tenant asked if the meeting date could be written down.
The housing options officer said he will print the meeting details and send them to the tenant.
The housing options officer said that if a notice or court letter is received, it will be sent to Moira on the same day.
The housing options officer said that the letter will be sent directly to him as well.
